intro: Maintenance workers fix almost anything, and that hands-on skill opens many specialized trades. The closest of the 25 careers below is Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics, Except Engines, with a 90% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $65,510, which is 32% more than the $49,590 maintenance and repair workers earn.
why_it_works: A typical day jumps from plumbing to electrical to machinery, figuring out what broke and how to fix it. O*NET rates equipment maintenance and repairing at 3.88 out of 5 for this job, and troubleshooting at 3.75. Specialized trades use those same skills on one type of system, often for much higher pay. All 25 matches need no extra schooling.
tips: Pick the system you enjoy fixing most and get certified in it; specialists earn far more than generalists.
Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers earn $109,910, which is 122% more, through apprenticeships.
Plumbing is a close 86% match with a median of $63,800, or 29% more.

faq.q: What jobs can former maintenance workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are mobile heavy equipment mechanics (90%), Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters (86%) and electric motor and power tool repairers (86%), based on O*NET 31.0. Farm equipment mechanics are 85% matched and earn $56,550, which is 14% more.

faq.q: Which careers for maintenance workers pay more?
faq.a: 21 of the 25 matches pay more than the $49,590 median. Elevator installers earn $109,910 (122% more), Ship Engineers $109,530 (121% more) and powerhouse and substation repairers $103,020 (108% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Most of them train through paid apprenticeships.

faq.q: Do maintenance workers need more education to switch trades?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than maintenance and repair workers already have. A post-secondary certificate is the most common level in the closest match, held by 55% of workers, so short programs and apprenticeships are the usual route.

faq.q: What skills should maintenance workers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, systems evaluation, operation and control and systems analysis. Complex problem solving already rates 3.12 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning to read and control systems is the main step up.
